subsections.title: Rudiments of Music
topics: Notation: Staff, Clefs (C, G, and F)
Scales (Western): Diatonic – Major and Minor (natural, harmonic and melodic); Chromatic (melodic only)
Modes (African): Pentatonic (5-tone), Hexatonic (6-tone), Heptatonic (7-tone)
Keys and Key Signatures
Time Signatures: Simple and Compound
Intervals
Transcription (Staff notation into Solfa and vice versa)
Transposition, including writing for transposing instruments
Musical terms, signs, ornaments and abbreviations

subsections.title: Elementary Harmony
topics: Chords/Triads: Primary (I/i, IV/iv, V and inversions), Secondary (ii, iii, vi and inversions), Chord vii° and inversions, Dominant 7th chords and inversions
Chord Progressions and Cadences (Perfect, Plagal, Interrupted, Imperfect) in major and minor keys
Use of primary and secondary triads in harmonising a given melody
Use of six-four chords (cadential and passing)
Non-harmonic tones: Passing (accented and non-accented), Auxiliary/Neighbouring tones, Anticipation

subsections.title: Counterpoint
topics: Two-part free Counterpoint (adding a part above or below a given melody)
Four-part harmony (SATB)

subsections.title: Composition
topics: Continuing a given melodic phrase in major or minor key (12-16 bars, possible modulation to closely related key)
Setting a given text in English to music

subsections.title: Form and Analysis
topics: Simple forms: binary, ternary, rondo, etc.
Extended forms: overture, oratorio, opera, cantata, suite, sonata, symphony, concerto, etc.
Form in traditional African music (antiphony: Call and Response, Cantor/Chorus, Call and Refrain; Repetitive/Cyclic forms, etc.)
Form in contemporary African art music (emphasis on melody, rhythm, harmony, instrumentation, through-composed pieces, etc.)
Analysis of prescribed set-works (Western or African) for each year

subsections.title: Aural Tests (Paper 3A)
topics: Rhythmic Dictation (up to 4 bars)
Melodic Dictation (up to 4 bars, may include African music elements)
Writing the upper or lower part of a two-part phrase
Identification of chords in a progression
Recognition of cadences
Recognition of modulations (to dominant, subdominant, relative major/minor)
Identification/Description of themes or excerpts (form, style, genre, instruments, scale/mode, meter)

subsections.title: Performance Test (Paper 3B)
topics: Performance on chosen instrument/voice: Voice (Soprano, Alto, Tenor, Baritone/Bass), Pianoforte/Electronic keyboard, Violin, Guitar, Recorder (descant/treble), Atenteben, Flute, B flat trumpet, E flat alto-saxophone, etc.
Sight-reading
Technical exercises, scales and arpeggios
Pieces from approved list

subsections.title: Western Music
subsections.composers: General knowledge of key composers and their contributions (e.g., Machaut, Palestrina, Bach, Handel, Mozart, Haydn, Beethoven, Schubert, Chopin, Wagner, Stravinsky, etc.)

subsections.title: Traditional and Contemporary African Art Music
topics: Role of music in traditional African society
Musical instruments: Names, description, classification, functions
General characteristics: Scales/Modes, Rhythm (cross-rhythm, hemiola, syncopation, polyrhythm), Polyphony, Form, Vocal styles, Texture, Instrumentation
Traditional vocal genres (dirges, lullabies, ritual songs, folk songs, satirical songs, etc.)
Traditional dances (Adowa, Kete, Atilogwu, Swange, etc.) and associated ethnic groups/occasions
Contemporary African Art Musicians (Nigeria and Ghana lists)

subsections.title: Popular African Music and Black Music in the Diaspora
topics: Popular musicians and genres in Nigeria and Ghana (Highlife, Juju, Fuji, Afrobeat, Hip-Hop, etc.)
Black Music in the Diaspora (Jazz, Blues, Gospel, Soul, Calypso, Reggae, etc. and key artists)

note: Set works for analysis and performance lists are updated annually by WAEC. Candidates should refer to the current year's prescribed works.
